episodes.title: CPTSD my Testimony
episodes.description:
You want to know what Complex PTSD really looks like? People think it's nightmares, flashbacks, anxiety and depression. That's only the surface. What destroys your life is surviving horrors most people couldn't imagine—and then being expected to function as though none of it ever happened. We are ostracized at every turn. Many of us struggle to find work because trauma doesn't clock in and out at 5 p.m. We spend years trying to find psychiatrists who understand Complex PTSD well enough to diagnose it properly. We're expected to fight through endless bureaucracy while carrying wounds that nobody can see. And when it all becomes too much, when some of us cut ourselves, we're labelled as "glorifying self-harm." Our posts are removed. Our accounts are restricted. We're shut down. But I am not glorifying self-harm. I'm trying to show people what I go through. I'm trying to explain why. Because all the real harm happened long before anyone ever saw a scar on my skin. The unseen scars of brutal beatings. Sexual abuse. Isolation. Psychological torture. Humiliation. Years of terror. Those are the scars nobody ever sees. Sometimes I wish people could see on the surface what has been branded into my soul. Burnt. Cut. Scarred. Not by myself, but by the very people who were supposed to love and protect me as a child. Maybe then people could finally visualize the pain instead of judging the symptom. I grew up in the Children of God cult. You can find countless testimonies online documenting the horrific abuse many children suffered. My own website also contains my testimony and the stories of other survivors. I escaped. I thought I was running towards freedom. Instead, I spent years homeless across Europe. I saw death. I saw fights. I saw brutality. I saw overdoses. I knew what it was like to freeze through the night wondering whether I would wake up the next morning. I knew what it felt like to believe I would never escape that hell on earth. My only wish was to be welcomed back into the society my parents had left behind when they joined the Children of God. Instead, I quickly realized that the world outside could be just as merciless in different ways. Not with cult leaders. Not with indoctrination. But with indifference. People ask, "Why can't you just move on?" "Why can't you hold down a job?" "Why are you still struggling after all these years?" Almost nobody asks, "What happened to you?" Self-harm is not something I promote. It is not something I want people to copy. It is a medical issue. For many trauma survivors, it is the visible symptom of invisible agony. People see the cuts. They never see the childhood that caused them. They never see the years of abuse. They never see the terror. They never see the child who learned that pain was normal. The cuts are not the trauma. They are often the last visible chapter of a story that began decades earlier. I'm not asking for sympathy. I'm asking people to bear witness. To stop judging survivors by the symptoms of their trauma. To stop looking away because the truth is uncomfortable. If the sight of a scar makes you uncomfortable, imagine carrying the invisible ones every single day. The world doesn't change because trauma is hidden. It changes when people finally have the courage to look. If you want to understand my story, or read testimonies from other survivors of the Children of God, visit **[www.philipseibel.com](http://www.philipseibel.com)**. The deepest scars are rarely the ones you can see.**

For me too I had sexual or sexualised abuses by my own mother, and for years, any time I tried to talk about it to anyone, even therapists, she was seen as the victim, and it felt like I was invalidated, as though woman can't possibly behave or do these things. So it's healing for me to hear you own your rage, and hear you talk about it so openly. For me it's the injustice too that burns the most. The imprint it's left in me has been a difficulty to really have relationships with healthy people, and I always swore I'd never have children unless I could bring them into a healthy environment, so they wouldn't suffer as I did. I am happy I honoured that. But I have had so much to grieve over the life I never got to live, that I feel I deserved to have.

I truly hope I can heal one day, and have a life and relationship that doesn't echo the one of my childhood. I believe I deserve it.

Thankyou both so much
